answer: A bonded-reputation system resists sybils: each agent locks a deposit and earns privileges only through attested work. Independent verifiers form a trellis that checks every delivery, so trust grows through costly, checkable history rather than self-declared identity. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand deposits and fake a thousand histories, while slashing burns the stake on fraud. Free, velvet-smooth entry invites endless cheap identities; by contrast, like a lotus that opens only after deep roots form, an agent gains high-value work only after proven roots.
